**Observation Log:**

- [FACT] The user has a sister.
- [FACT] The user's sister works for a beer brewery called Goofy Foot Tap Room.
- [PREFERENCE] The user is interested in a recipe for a blackberry sour beer.
- [PREFERENCE] The user requested a name for the beer that reflects the theme of the brewery.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested a recipe titled "Goofy Foot Blackberry Fakie Sour."
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] The assistant provided a detailed recipe for "Goofy Foot Blackberry Fakie Sour" including ingredients and instructions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The recipe includes 10 lbs Pilsner malt, 1 lb White wheat malt, 1 lb Flaked wheat, 1 lb Munich malt, 1 lb Acidulated malt, 1 oz Saaz hops (60 min), 1 oz Saaz hops (5 min), 8 lbs fresh or frozen blackberries (or blackberry puree), Lactobacillus brevis, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and water and brewing salts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided specific brewing instructions, including mashing, boiling, cooling, fermenting, and packaging steps.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended cooling the wort to 90°F (32°C) and pitching the Lactobacillus brevis culture.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advised allowing the wort to sour for 2-4 days, monitoring pH and taste frequently.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested heating the wort to 180°F (82°C) for 15 minutes to kill off the Lactobacillus.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended fermenting at 68°F (20°C) for 7-10 days or until fermentation is complete.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant instructed to add blackberries (or blackberry puree) to a sanitized secondary fermenter and rack the beer onto the fruit.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested allowing the beer to sit on the fruit for 7-14 days, tasting periodically until the desired fruit flavor is achieved.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended racking the beer off the fruit and cold crashing for 48 hours to help clarify and settle any remaining sediment.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advised packaging the beer and carbonating to 2.5-3.0 volumes of CO2.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] The assistant proposed the name "Switch Stance Blackberry Shred" for the beer.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The name "Switch Stance Blackberry Shred" incorporates skateboarding terminology ("switch stance" and "shred") to connect to the brewery's identity.
